section_summary.extract_value: The current study examined associations between body appreciation and measures of need for uniqueness and interest in cosmetic enhancements. Results indicated that higher body appreciation was significantly associated with greater need for uniqueness both generally and regarding appearance (effects held after accounting for sex, BMI, and race/ethnicity), but was not significantly associated with interest in cosmetic enhancements. Regression results also showed that African Americans/Blacks had significantly higher need for uniqueness in general and in appearance.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The goal of the current study was to explore associations between body appreciation and variables that reflect self-enhancement and/or self-expression, including interest in cosmetic enhancements and need for uniqueness." "Body appreciation was associated with a greater desire for uniqueness both generally and in the domain of appearance; these findings emerged once the effects of sex, BMI, and race/ethnicity had been accounted for." "Body appreciation was not significantly associated with interest in cosmetic enhancements." "Results from the regressions also showed that African Americans/Blacks had significantly higher need for uniqueness, both generally and in the domain of appearance."
